text: oh and speaking of that 'wgsl compiles' i will say, so we just went from like 103 -> 400+ of them, and the very first startup after the massive increase was no shit like 2 minutes before i ever got a window. I have to assume, during that time, it was compiling all the shaders. because its now back to instant startups, but doesnt explain the possible re-compiling if that is the case
resolution: The 2-minute first boot after the 103->400 shader jump was the GPU driver compiling the single generated fill megashader (all 400+ material functions live in ONE ~700KB WGSL module) on first pipeline creation; Mesa's on-disk shader cache absorbs that on later boots, which is why startups went back to instant. The recurring per-page cost was NOT driver recompilation but wgpu's synchronous WGSL parse/validate in createShaderModule, which effects.zig re-ran for every Effect instance because pipelines were never actually shared. Fixed by the process-wide pipeline cache in 3a648d752: the megashader is parsed once per source change per run, then every thumb/picker mount reuses the cached pipeline.
